incident: HTML Smuggling Leads to Domain Wide Nokoyawa Ransomware (12 hours)

sources.title: HTML Smuggling Leads to Domain Wide Ransomware - The DFIR Report (2023-08-28)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (HTML smuggling ZIP/ISO/LNK -> IcedID via rundll32), hops (RDP to DC with CS DLL, RDP to backup server + file server, netscan, PsExec/WMIC), cred access (LSASS via CS, SessionGopher on DC), impact (Nokoyawa k.exe + p.bat via PsExec/WMIC domain-wide), TTR 12h

narrative_before: In an early-November 2022 intrusion (published 2023) the DFIR Report observed TA551 thread-hijacked email delivering an HTML-smuggling file: a fake Adobe page downloaded a password-protected ZIP containing an ISO whose only visible file was a LNK (documents-9771). Clicking it ran commands copying rundll32 and a malicious DLL and executing IcedID (hourly scheduled-task persistence). ~3h after execution a cmd process beaconed to a Cobalt Strike server (seen in a prior Nokoyawa report), accessed LSASS and checked domain admins. After a ~3h pause the actor looked up specific domain admins and used one account to RDP to a domain controller, copying a CS beacon (1.dll) and running it. AdFind (via batch) and nslookup-per-host ran on the DC; ~5h later SessionGopher ran, and the actor RDPed to a backup server and a file server. Back on the DC, netscan ran and PsExec/WMIC copied k.exe (Nokoyawa) and p.bat across hosts. Five minutes later Nokoyawa ran on the DC and PsExec started p.bat on the other hosts; time to ransomware was just over 12 hours.

detection_moments.description: IcedID executed via HTML-smuggled ISO/LNK/rundll32 on the beachhead; ~3h later Cobalt Strike beacon + LSASS access.
detection_moments.evidence: 'When the user clicked the LNK file ... executing the malware ... a connection was made to IcedID command and control servers ... observed accessing LSASS' - HTML Smuggling, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: Actor RDPs to a domain controller using a domain admin account, copies and runs a Cobalt Strike DLL, runs AdFind and SessionGopher.
detection_moments.evidence: 'initiated a RDP session to move laterally to a domain controller ... copied over a Cobalt Strike beacon to the domain controller and executed it ... SessionGopher' - HTML Smuggling

detection_moments.description: RDP to backup and file servers; netscan on the DC; PsExec/WMIC copy k.exe + p.bat; Nokoyawa runs on the DC and via PsExec on other hosts (TTR 12h).
detection_moments.evidence: 'both PsExec and WMIC were used to move files ... k.exe and p.bat ... the Nokoyawa ransomware binary was executed on a domain controller ... PsExec was used to execute the p.bat file starting the ransomware binary on the other hosts' - HTML Smuggling

attack_path: HTML smuggling ZIP/ISO/LNK runs IcedID via rundll32 (T1566.001/T1204.002)
RDP to a domain controller with a domain admin account; CS DLL copied and run (T1021.001)
RDP from DC to backup server (backup console opened) (T1021.001)
RDP from DC to file server (file reviewed) (T1021.001)
PsExec/WMIC copy k.exe + p.bat and run Nokoyawa domain-wide (T1021.002/T1486)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role only; victim sector not stated. 'Other hosts in the domain' modelled as srv_1/pc_2.
No exfiltration described (LSASS access via CS; data staging not detailed).
Moments are the report's own timeline markers (IcedID+CS, DC RDP, encryption), not a defender detection timeline.
